correctness.rationale: The Newton–Schulz residual squares exactly, so scalar initialization gives X_k=q_m(A) with m=2^k. On the spectral convergence interval q_m is positive; for even m it is strictly decreasing. In two dimensions, q_m(A)=c_0 I+c_1 A with c_1<=0, so a Stieltjes off-diagonal becomes nonnegative and positive definiteness supplies positive diagonals. The 3x3 rational witness has A>0 and 2I-A>0 by exact leading principal minors, hence rho(I-A)<1; exact multiplication gives A^{-1}>0, X_1>=0, and (X_2)_{13}=-1/500.

value.rationale: For Stieltjes matrices the exact inverse is entrywise nonnegative, and Newton–Schulz approximate inverses are used in preconditioning. A minimal-dimension theorem identifies exactly when convergent intermediate approximants can first create a wrong-signed coupling. The strict 3x3 rational witness is robust and small enough to serve as a diagnostic example; the result is structural rather than a routine numerical recomputation.
